time.desc: Country Y announces tariffs on all imports from neighboring Country W to pressure it to stem illegal immigration
Country Y The head of the central bank publicly criticized the decision to raise taxes on Country W as a huge mistake
A logistics company sued the government of Country Y to block technology export restrictions targeting Company H
Country J officially passed the digital services tax bill, becoming the first country in Region A to levy this tax
Country Y launches trade investigation and threatens retaliation over Country J’s digital services tax
Country Y announced that it will impose additional tariffs on another large number of imported goods (hundreds of billions of dollars) Country X
Country X Diplomats responded that imposing additional tariffs is by no means the correct way to resolve economic and trade frictions
Country Y announced to postpone the tax increase on some Country X products to avoid impacting the country’s consumers during the shopping season.

The ruling party's tariffs on all imported goods from neighboring countries will be raised in stages. If the border crisis continues, they will be increased month by month, up to a maximum of 25% and maintained until the other party takes effective action.
The ruling government says it plans to seek legislative approval for a new trade deal with neighboring countries.

Country X The authorities have basically completed the preparations for including the logistics company on the list of unreliable entities. Affected by this news, the company's stock price fell that day.
The ruling party’s trade department launched a regulatory investigation into the Country J digital services tax, which has been used to impose tariffs on countries that harm national interests.

Country J The Finance Minister publicly defended the digital services tax, emphasized that the country has the sovereignty to independently determine tax rules, and called on the ruling party to speed up an agreement on an international digital tax.

Regional Organization A The original plan for a unified digital tax was shelved due to opposition from some member states. Country J The unilateral advancement made it isolated within the organization.

The ruling party has imposed a 25% tariff on approximately 250 billion U.S. dollars of imported goods from Country X. After the implementation of the new round of tariffs, almost all imported goods from Country X will be covered.

The leader of the ruling party said that the promotion of new tariffs was a punishment for Country X's failure to fulfill its commitments, including failure to purchase more agricultural products and failure to prevent the inflow of fentanyl

The trade department of the ruling party said that some Country X products are exempted from tariffs due to health, safety, national security and other factors, and some have been deferred due to their significant impact on the country’s economy.
Retail industry groups welcome the decision to postpone the tax increase, but emphasize that comprehensive elimination of tariffs is the fundamental solution
